paper.title: Questioning the Coverage-Length Metric in Conformal Prediction: When Shorter Intervals Are Not Better

C1.summary: 16/16 nontrivial bias-20 synthetic alpha/p conditions are shorter; maximum aggregate coverage error is 0.013.

C2.summary: Current source matches clean-room exactly and bias-10 matches the historical CSV to 7.1e-15, but the paper p=.96 PT length is not exact.

C3.summary: Seven obtainable datasets ran and all seven are shorter; the full paper 9/10 dataset claim is not rerun.

C4.summary: 80 stochastic PT rows are positive and two-outcome; 20 p=1 controls are deterministic; no false positives or negatives.

C5_constructive.summary: 15/15 conditions, 1.5 million retrainings, zero samplewise mismatches, and a passing independent audit.

C5_trained_localizer.summary: Three data seeds and twenty retrains per seed yield positive localized IS, VCP IS zero, and mean coverage 0.90625.

full_paper_experiments.summary: Theorem proofs, unavailable datasets/checkpoints, classification tasks, full ablations, and complete paper tables are outside the committed audit.
